thread.title_full: Waterford downs South Windsor to win American Legion state tournament championship - NewsBreak

title: Waterford downs South Windsor to win American Legion state tournament championship - NewsBreak
text:
MIDDLETOWN —The Waterford American Legion baseball team was perfect in Zone 6 play this summer and was even better during the state tournament. And the players say they're not done yet. Trace Morales fired a four-hitter and Alex Dreyfus went 3-for-3 with three RBIs and two runs scored as top-seeded Waterford earned its first state championship in 17 years by defeating No. 2 South Windsor 8-1 at Palmer Field Wednesday. "We as a team play better when we're under pressure," Dreyfus said. "A lot of us returned from last year and we were pretty good last year. When we play good competition we thrive." Waterford advances to the eight-team, double-elimination Northeast Regional at Fitton Field on the campus of Holy Cross in Worcester Aug. 6-10 and faces host Shrewsbury in the final game of Day 1. The Legion World Series is scheduled for Aug. 14-19 in Shelby, North Carolina. The state title is Waterford's second to go with its first one won in 2008. "This is huge," Morales said. "Everyone pitched in. We played more with a chip on our shoulder here. We came together as a team." Morales, who attends and plays at Southern Connecticut State University, was named the tournament's Most Valuable Player. The right-hander walked none, struck out five, and retired the last 11 batters he faced. His defense, led by shortstop Alex Picardi, was outstanding. "He consistently threw strikes," Waterford coach Joe Mariani said. "He got his curve ball over and kept them off-balance. And we made some nice plays behind him. As the game went on, he got better. He was great tonight." South Windsor's second-place showing is its best in program history. It finished third in 1998. The Zone 3 champions' offense carried it far but Morales was in control as Waterford defeated South Windsor for the second time in three days. "I knew they were an aggressive team and very scrappy," Morales said. "I knew they wanted to win so I guess I wanted it more. We had a game plan coming in and we executed in." The start of the game was delayed 45 minutes due to rain. Waterford wasted no time taking the lead. South Windsor's Jake Gombotz, who had opened tournament play with shutouts of Glastonbury and Ridgefield, gave up a one-out triple to Matt Shampine and he scored on a single by Dreyfus. After a single by Martin Light, Picardi's single plated Dreyfus for a 2-0 lead. "We had a good amount of momentum coming in but it was really important to keep it going," Dreyfus said of the fast start. Nate Jolly got South Windsor on the board with an RBI double in the second. Waterford responded in the third as Donte Valentine's double brought home Dreyfus. Waterford made it 4-1 on Dreyfus' third hit, a bloop single in the fourth and iced it with a four-run sixth against reliever Sam Balducci with three of the runs being unearned due to two errors. Picardi added two hits and two RBIs for Waterford. South Windsor's Logan Sinacola was named the tournament's top hitter while Waterford's Shampine was selected the tournament's top pitcher. Waterford has lost in non-zone play this summer but heads to Worcester and the regional on a roll. It has six days to prepare. "Rest, and just stay sharp," Mariani said of the most important things his team needs to do during its break. "We'll give the kids a couple of days off. I like the way we've been playing. We've been playing awesome. I'm very happy with where we're at so I think we've got a good shot." Prior to the game, South Windsor's Balducci was awarded a $1,000 scholarship by the American Legion. Balducci, a 2025 South Windsor High graduate, will attend the University of Saint Joseph in West Hartford in the fall. Trace Morales, Waterford. Limited South Windsor to one run and four hits in a complete-game effort. He struck out five. "Legion is the epitome of baseball, in my opinion. Every game means something. This tournament is wonderful. The kids compete every pitch of every inning. It's unlike any tournament you can ever play in. It's a hard tournament to win. It's a true accomplishment." -- Waterford coach Joe Mariani. (at Palmer Field, Middletown) SOUTH WINDSOR 010 000 0 - 1 4 2
